## Goals

SCGSim is an independent downstream toolkit for research-stable,
superconducting-circuit simulation workflows. Its direction is:

- one explicit geometry-to-results contract across supported solvers;
- public, reviewable provenance and failure behavior;
- notebook-first workflows that stay readable to researchers;
- results-first feedback to the [gsim community](https://github.com/gdsfactory/gsim)
  through public fixtures and evidence;
- Agent-driven development with exact revision and validation records.

## V1 acceptance and delivery {#v1-acceptance-and-delivery}

On 2026-10-05 the Human explicitly accepted the complete implemented V1
semantics and assigned bounded stabilization. Acceptance covers the current
geometry, supported solver workflows, result ownership, failure contracts,
retained numerical/geometry policies and documented limitations, including
caller-owned whole sweep counts, native convergence observations and narrow
Palace native infinite-Q handling. The linked technical contracts remain the
authority for exact behavior; acceptance adds no scientific adequacy threshold
or support for excluded backends.

The semantic state is **STABILIZED**: the Human-assigned minimal checks have
passed independent review and preserve the accepted function and failure
behavior. They do not establish universal physics accuracy or new native
solver evidence. Stable `main` carries the latest stable release, while `develop` carries the
next prerelease line. Integration, Pages deployment and workspace synchronization
keep their own recorded identities; semantic stabilization alone does not
publish a newer version.
Historical receipts retain their original source, outcome and evidence scope.

Native Askr presentation is confirmed for the 1.0.1 maintenance release:
four Areas, Pages and Sections navigation, and versioned sites that distinguish
original content from presentation. Release delivery is authorized;
instructional content revisions remain separate and are not accepted by this
presentation decision. Runtime, result and scientific semantics remain
unchanged. A historical version keeps its original authored content and source
revision; updated presentation is recorded separately.

## Non-goals

SCGSim does not:

- claim to be official gsim or replace upstream gsim;
- promise that every code change receives Human review;
- automatically accept upstream gsim APIs as SCGSim APIs;
- maintain compatibility shims for older experimental interfaces;
- support Meep;
- use an external gsim runner or cloud execution as a fallback;
- publish private designs, controls, paths, or run artifacts.

## Starting-source identities

The integrated starting lane is:

| Authority | Exact identity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| gsim downstream source | `0.2.0+scq.1`, `main@8f5dc6c05255d003a9c6d8959537bcf8068379d3`, tree `505a53741953666da17d81b7036eba3ac296cd1a` | Source input for selective downstream integration; not automatic SCGSim API acceptance. |
| Semantic Geometry Builder | `e74a343154c6b19b6ba32d6fb297e700cfe08ff2` | Derivation provenance only; the in-tree `scgsim.sgb` Core is the current geometry and topology authority consumed by SCGSim. |

These identities establish provenance only. They imply neither a numerical
Surface-EPR result nor a live Palace solve, a new direct external consumer, or
a fallback path.

## Upstream feedback

The default feedback route is public fixtures, evidence, and concrete findings.
Upstream source contribution is optional and case-specific rather than the
definition of downstream success.
